title: Exodus Chapter 40 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Exodus chapter 40 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Exodus Chapter 40 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Exodus Chapter 40.

questions.question: On which day and month was Moses commanded to set up the tabernacle?
options: The first day of the first month
The tenth day of the first month
The first day of the second month
The tenth day of the second month
questions.correctAnswer: The first day of the first month
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:2 states that Moses was to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month.

questions.question: What was Moses instructed to put inside the tabernacle first?
options: The ark of the testimony
The table
The candlestick
The altar of burnt offering
questions.correctAnswer: The ark of the testimony
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:3 commands Moses to put the ark of the testimony inside the tabernacle first.

questions.question: True or False: Moses was told to light the lamps on the candlestick after bringing it into the tabernacle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:4 instructs Moses to bring in the candlestick and light its lamps.

questions.question: Where was the altar of gold for incense to be placed?
options: Before the ark of the testimony
Outside the tabernacle
In the court gate
Next to the laver
questions.correctAnswer: Before the ark of the testimony
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:5 states that the altar of gold for incense was to be set before the ark of the testimony.

questions.question: True or False: The altar of burnt offering was to be placed inside the tabernacle.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:6 says the altar of burnt offering was placed before the door of the tabernacle, not inside it.

questions.question: What was placed between the tent of the congregation and the altar?
options: The laver filled with water
The altar of incense
The table of showbread
The candlestick
questions.correctAnswer: The laver filled with water
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:7 details that the laver was set between the tent and the altar and filled with water.

questions.question: What was Moses commanded to do with the anointing oil?
options: Anoint the tabernacle and all that was therein
Anoint only the priests
Anoint the altar of burnt offering only
Anoint the children of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Anoint the tabernacle and all that was therein
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:9 commands Moses to anoint the tabernacle, all that is therein, and all its vessels.

questions.question: What is the status given to the altar of burnt offering after anointing?
options: An altar most holy
An ordinary altar
A temporary altar
A burnt altar
questions.correctAnswer: An altar most holy
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:10 states that after anointing, the altar shall be an altar most holy.

questions.question: True or False: The laver and its foot were to be anointed and sanctified.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:11 instructs Moses to anoint and sanctify the laver and its foot.

questions.question: Who was to be brought to the door of the tabernacle to be washed with water?
options: Aaron and his sons
Moses and Aaron
All the Levites
The elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Aaron and his sons
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:12 directs Moses to bring Aaron and his sons to the door of the tabernacle and wash them with water.

questions.question: What garments were put on Aaron before he was anointed and sanctified?
options: Holy garments
Coats
Robes of many colors
Simple linen clothes
questions.correctAnswer: Holy garments
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:13 states Aaron was clothed with holy garments before being anointed and sanctified.

questions.question: What was the purpose of anointing Aaron and his sons?
options: That they may minister in the priest's office
To make them kings
To send them as spies
To consecrate them as prophets
questions.correctAnswer: That they may minister in the priest's office
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:13 explains the anointing was so Aaron could minister in the priest's office.

questions.question: True or False: The anointing of Aaron's sons was described as an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:15 clearly states the anointing of Aaron's sons is an everlasting priesthood through generations.

questions.question: Which instruction comes first in Exodus 40:2-13?
options: Set up the tabernacle of the tent of congregation
Bring Aaron and his sons to wash
Anoint the altar of burnt offering
Put the table and set in order the things on it
questions.correctAnswer: Set up the tabernacle of the tent of congregation
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:2 shows the first instruction is to set up the tabernacle before other tasks like anointing or bringing Aaron and his sons.

questions.question: What was done to the altar of burnt offering before it was sanctified?
options: It was anointed with oil
It was covered with a vail
It was filled with water
It was set outside the camp
questions.correctAnswer: It was anointed with oil
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:10 commands anointing the altar of burnt offering before sanctifying it.

medium.title: Exodus Chapter 40 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Exodus Chapter 40 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Exodus 40:14-15, what was the purpose of anointing Aaron's sons as Moses anointed their father?
options: To serve as priests and establish an everlasting priesthood
To become prophets in Israel
To lead the tribes of Israel in battle
To build the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: To serve as priests and establish an everlasting priesthood
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:14-15 explains that Aaron's sons were clothed and anointed just like their father so they could minister in the priest's office, and their anointing would be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

questions.question: What does Exodus 40:16 teach about Moses' obedience to God's commands?
options: Moses followed all of the LORD’s commands exactly as given
Moses altered some commands to fit the situation
Moses delayed following the LORD’s commands
Moses asked others to carry out the commands for him
questions.correctAnswer: Moses followed all of the LORD’s commands exactly as given
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:16 states that Moses did everything exactly as the LORD commanded him, showing full obedience and trust in God's instructions.

questions.question: On what day was the tabernacle erected according to Exodus 40:17?
options: The first day of the first month in the second year
The tenth day of the first month in the second year
The first day of the second month in the first year
The tenth day of the second month in the first year
questions.correctAnswer: The first day of the first month in the second year
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:17 specifies that the tabernacle was reared up on the first day of the first month in the second year, emphasizing the fulfillment of God's timing.

questions.question: According to Exodus 40:18-19, what steps did Moses take to set up the tabernacle?
options: He fastened sockets, set up the boards and bars, reared pillars, and spread the tent covering
He built a stone altar and painted the walls
He gathered animals for sacrifice and prayed for guidance
He wrote down the laws and taught the people
questions.correctAnswer: He fastened sockets, set up the boards and bars, reared pillars, and spread the tent covering
questions.explanation: Verses 18-19 describe Moses physically assembling the tabernacle by fastening sockets, setting up boards and bars, rearing pillars, and spreading the tent covering as the LORD commanded.

questions.question: Where was the testimony placed inside the tabernacle as described in Exodus 40:20-21?
options: In the ark with staves and mercy seat, covered by the vail
On the altar of burnt offering
On the table of showbread
Near the laver of water
questions.correctAnswer: In the ark with staves and mercy seat, covered by the vail
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:20-21 explains the testimony was placed inside the ark, with its staves and mercy seat, and then the ark was brought into the tabernacle and covered with the vail, showing reverence and separation.

questions.question: How were the table and bread arranged inside the tabernacle according to Exodus 40:22-23?
options: The table was placed on the north side without the vail, and bread was set before the LORD
The table was placed outside the tabernacle, and no bread was used
The table was placed in the courtyard, and bread was burnt as an offering
The table was placed on the south side, and bread was hidden
questions.correctAnswer: The table was placed on the north side without the vail, and bread was set before the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 22-23 describe that the table was put on the north side within the tent but outside the vail, and the bread was arranged there before the LORD, symbolizing provision and fellowship.

questions.question: According to Exodus 40:24-25, what was the position and function of the candlestick in the tabernacle?
options: Placed on the south side opposite the table, with lamps lit before the LORD
Placed at the entrance to the courtyard, with lamps extinguished
Placed on the north side beside the altar, unlit
Placed outside the tabernacle, as decoration
questions.correctAnswer: Placed on the south side opposite the table, with lamps lit before the LORD
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:24-25 indicates the candlestick was placed on the south side opposite the table and its lamps were lit before the LORD, symbolizing light and guidance.

questions.question: What was the significance of the golden altar according to Exodus 40:26-27?
options: It was placed before the vail and used to burn sweet incense
It was used for burnt offerings outside the courtyard
It was a decorative piece with no function
It was used to wash the priests
questions.correctAnswer: It was placed before the vail and used to burn sweet incense
questions.explanation: Verses 26-27 explain that the golden altar was set before the vail inside the tabernacle and was used for burning sweet incense, symbolizing prayer and worship.

questions.question: Where was the altar of burnt offering located and what was done there according to Exodus 40:28-29?
options: By the door of the tabernacle, where burnt and meat offerings were made
Inside the holy of holies, where incense was burned
On the north side near the table, used for washing hands
Outside the camp, for animal sacrifices
questions.correctAnswer: By the door of the tabernacle, where burnt and meat offerings were made
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:28-29 states that the altar of burnt offering was placed by the door of the tabernacle and offerings were made upon it, highlighting obedience and atonement.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the laver according to Exodus 40:30-32?
options: To provide water for washing hands and feet before entering the tent or near the altar
To hold the bread of the presence
To store the anointing oil
To serve as a basin for burnt offerings
questions.correctAnswer: To provide water for washing hands and feet before entering the tent or near the altar
questions.explanation: Verses 30-32 describe the laver being set between the tent and altar with water for washing hands and feet, emphasizing cleanliness and preparation before ministering.

questions.question: What does the cloud covering the tent of the congregation and the glory of the LORD filling the tabernacle symbolize in Exodus 40:34-35?
options: God's presence and approval upon the tabernacle
A sign of impending disaster
The end of the Israelites' journey
The absence of God
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence and approval upon the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:34-35 describes the cloud and glory filling the tabernacle as a visible sign of God's presence, sanctifying the place and showing His approval.

questions.question: True or False: Exodus 40:19 states that Moses spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering above it, following the LORD’s command.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:19 explicitly says Moses spread the tent over the tabernacle and put the covering upon it as the LORD commanded, demonstrating obedience.

questions.question: True or False: According to Exodus 40:31-32, Moses and Aaron did not wash their hands and feet before ministering in the tent.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:31-32 clearly states that Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet at the laver before entering the tent or approaching the altar, demonstrating ritual purity and obedience.

questions.question: According to Exodus 40:36-38, what determined when the Israelites would journey onward?
options: Whether the cloud covering the tabernacle lifted
The phase of the moon
The priests’ decision
After a fixed number of days
questions.correctAnswer: Whether the cloud covering the tabernacle lifted
questions.explanation: Verses 36-38 describe that the Israelites only journeyed when the cloud lifted from the tabernacle, showing reliance on God's guidance and timing.

questions.question: How does Exodus 40:14-15 teach about the virtue of faithfulness in Christian living?
options: It shows the importance of faithful service through generations by establishing an everlasting priesthood
It emphasizes personal ambition over service
It encourages ignoring traditions
It promotes individualism without community
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the importance of faithful service through generations by establishing an everlasting priesthood
questions.explanation: The anointing of Aaron’s sons as priests in verses 14-15 teaches faithfulness in serving God continuously and passing down spiritual responsibilities, encouraging believers to be faithful in their calling.

hard.title: Exodus Chapter 40 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Exodus Chapter 40.

questions.question: What was burned on the golden altar before the veil in the tabernacle as commanded by the LORD?
options: Sweet incense
Burnt offering
Meat offering
Olive oil
questions.correctAnswer: Sweet incense
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:27 states that Moses burnt sweet incense on the golden altar before the veil, fulfilling the LORD's command.

questions.question: Where was the altar of burnt offering placed according to Moses' setting up of the tabernacle?
options: By the door of the tabernacle
Inside the holy place
In the outer court, opposite the laver
On the north side of the tabernacle
questions.correctAnswer: By the door of the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:29 details that the altar of burnt offering was placed by the door of the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation, as commanded by the LORD.

questions.question: What was the purpose of the laver set between the tent of the congregation and the altar?
options: To hold water for washing
To hold incense
To store the holy garments
To burn offerings
questions.correctAnswer: To hold water for washing
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:30 explains that the laver was set between the tent and the altar, and water was put in it to wash withal, symbolizing purification before entering the holy place.

questions.question: Who washed their hands and feet at the laver as described in Exodus 40?
options: Moses, Aaron, and his sons
Only Aaron
The entire congregation
Moses and the elders of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Moses, Aaron, and his sons
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:31 specifies that Moses, Aaron, and his sons washed their hands and feet at the laver before ministering, signifying ritual cleanliness.

questions.question: What signified the glory of the LORD filling the tabernacle upon its completion?
options: A cloud covering the tent of the congregation
A pillar of smoke by day
A bright star appearing above
Thunder and lightning
questions.correctAnswer: A cloud covering the tent of the congregation
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:34 records that a cloud covered the tent of the congregation and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle, indicating divine presence.

questions.question: Why was Moses unable to enter the tent of the congregation after the glory of the LORD filled it?
options: Because the cloud abode thereon
Because it was locked
Because he was not anointed
Because Aaron forbade him
questions.correctAnswer: Because the cloud abode thereon
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:35 explains that Moses could not enter the tent because the cloud remained on it and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle, showing divine holiness.

questions.question: What determined when the children of Israel would journey onward during their travels?
options: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle
When the priests blew the trumpets
When the sun rose in the east
When Moses gave the command
questions.correctAnswer: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:36-37 state that Israel journeyed only when the cloud covering the tabernacle was lifted, indicating divine guidance on their travels.

questions.question: What was the significance of the cloud by day and fire by night over the tabernacle in the sight of all Israel?
options: It was the visible sign of the LORD's presence throughout their journeys
It was a natural weather phenomenon
It signified the changing seasons
It represented the power of Moses
questions.correctAnswer: It was the visible sign of the LORD's presence throughout their journeys
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:38 clarifies that the cloud by day and fire by night symbolized the LORD's presence among Israel during all their journeys.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of divine presence symbolized by cloud and fire as in Exodus 40?
options: Leviticus 9:23-24
Genesis 1:2
Psalm 23:4
Isaiah 53:5
questions.correctAnswer: Leviticus 9:23-24
questions.explanation: Leviticus 9:23-24 describes the glory of the LORD appearing as fire upon the altar after Moses and Aaron's offerings, paralleling the divine presence symbolized by cloud and fire in Exodus 40:34-38.

questions.question: How does the anointing of Aaron and his sons in Exodus 40 relate to the New Testament concept of priesthood?
options: It prefigures the eternal priesthood of Jesus Christ
It contradicts the priesthood in Hebrews
It represents a temporary role abolished later
It is unrelated to New Testament teachings
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures the eternal priesthood of Jesus Christ
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:15 speaks of an everlasting priesthood through Aaron's lineage, which the New Testament book of Hebrews (Hebrews 7:23-28) fulfills by presenting Jesus as the eternal high priest.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'tabernacle' in Exodus 40, and what does it signify?
options: Mishkan, meaning 'dwelling place' signifying God's presence among His people
Sanctum, meaning 'holy place' signifying separation
Ohel, meaning 'tent' signifying temporary shelter
Beit, meaning 'house' signifying permanence
questions.correctAnswer: Mishkan, meaning 'dwelling place' signifying God's presence among His people
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word for tabernacle is 'Mishkan,' which means 'dwelling place,' emphasizing that the tabernacle was designed as God's residence among Israel (Exodus 40:2).

questions.question: What literary device is primarily used in Exodus 40:34-38 to emphasize the LORD's guidance and presence?
options: Inclusio framing the narrative with cloud and fire
Metaphor comparing the cloud to a throne
Chiasm focusing on Moses' inability to enter
Parable illustrating Israel's journey
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio framing the narrative with cloud and fire
questions.explanation: The passage uses an inclusio literary device by beginning and ending with references to the cloud and fire symbolizing God's presence and guidance (Exodus 40:34 and 40:38).

questions.question: How does the setting up of the tabernacle in Exodus 40 fulfill earlier instructions given to Moses?
options: It was done exactly as the LORD commanded, completing the divine plan
It was partially done with some modifications by Moses
It was delayed and incomplete
It was rejected by the Israelites
questions.correctAnswer: It was done exactly as the LORD commanded, completing the divine plan
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:16 states that Moses did everything according to the LORD's commands, fulfilling the instructions given since Exodus 25, thus completing God's plan for worship.

questions.question: True or False: Moses anointed only the tabernacle and not the altar or laver in Exodus 40.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:9-11 records that Moses anointed the tabernacle, altar of burnt offering, and the laver, sanctifying all these for holy use.

questions.question: True or False: The cloud and fire that covered the tabernacle were visible signs to all the house of Israel throughout their journeys.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:38 explains that the cloud by day and fire by night were in the sight of all Israel, demonstrating God's continual presence and guidance.

theological.title: Exodus Chapter 40 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Exodus Chapter 40 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What was the first step commanded by the LORD on the first day of the first month in the second year?
options: Set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation
Anoint Aaron and his sons as priests
Offer burnt offerings on the altar
Light the lamps of the candlestick
questions.correctAnswer: Set up the tabernacle of the tent of the congregation
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:2 commands Moses to set up the tabernacle on the first day of the first month, indicating the foundational act of establishing God's dwelling place among Israel.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the anointing of the tabernacle, its vessels, and the priests as described in Exodus 40:9-15?
options: Sanctification and the setting apart of persons and things for holy service
Justification by faith alone
The doctrine of the Trinity
The perseverance of the saints
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and the setting apart of persons and things for holy service
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:9-15 describes the anointing and sanctifying of the tabernacle, vessels, Aaron, and his sons, illustrating the doctrine of sanctification—God setting apart people and objects for His holy use.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated by the cloud covering the tent and the glory filling the tabernacle in Exodus 40:34?
options: God’s holiness and glory dwelling among His people
God’s wrath against sin
God’s omniscience
God’s justice in judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s holiness and glory dwelling among His people
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:34 shows the cloud covering the tent and the glory of the LORD filling the tabernacle, revealing God's holy presence dwelling visibly with His covenant people.

questions.question: How does Exodus 40:12-15 contribute to the biblical theology of priesthood?
options: It establishes the hereditary and perpetual priesthood of Aaron's descendants
It teaches the priesthood of all believers
It abolishes the priesthood in favor of prophets
It introduces the Levitical priesthood as temporary
questions.correctAnswer: It establishes the hereditary and perpetual priesthood of Aaron's descendants
questions.explanation: Verses 12-15 describe the anointing of Aaron and his sons and declare their priesthood 'everlasting,' establishing the hereditary nature of the Aaronic priesthood as a type pointing forward to Christ’s eternal priesthood (Hebrews 7).

questions.question: In Exodus 40:7 and 40:30, the laver is placed between the altar and the tent. What doctrine does this placement symbolize?
options: The necessity of purification before approaching God
The omnipresence of God
The final judgment of humanity
The sovereignty of God over creation
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of purification before approaching God
questions.explanation: The laver, placed between the altar of burnt offering and the tent (Exodus 40:7, 30), symbolizes the essential purification (washing) required before one can draw near to God, reflecting the doctrine of sanctification and cleansing from sin.

questions.question: What is the significance of Moses not being able to enter the tent because the cloud and glory of the LORD filled it (Exodus 40:35)?
options: It reveals the overwhelming holiness of God that even the mediator must approach with reverence
It indicates God's anger towards Moses
It shows that the tabernacle was incomplete
It implies that Moses was unworthy to lead Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the overwhelming holiness of God that even the mediator must approach with reverence
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:35 highlights God's overwhelming holiness and glory filling the tabernacle, making it impossible for Moses to enter, underscoring the need for reverence and the mediator’s role between a holy God and sinful humanity.

questions.question: Which combined teaching do Exodus 40:26-27 and Exodus 40:5 convey about the role of incense and the altar in worship?
options: Incense symbolizes the prayers of the saints ascending to God, and the altar is the place of atonement and worship
Incense represents the law, and the altar is for sacrifices only
Incense is purely decorative, and the altar is for judgment
Incense is for cleansing, and the altar is symbolic of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Incense symbolizes the prayers of the saints ascending to God, and the altar is the place of atonement and worship
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:26-27 describes burning incense on the golden altar before the ark, while 40:5 positions the altar before the ark; combined these show the altar as the locus of atonement and worship, and incense typifies prayers rising to God (cf. Psalm 141:2).

questions.question: How does the description of the cloud and fire over the tabernacle in Exodus 40:36-38 function in the narrative arc of Israel’s journey?
options: It represents God’s continual guidance and presence during Israel’s wilderness journey
It indicates God’s abandonment of Israel
It shows the fragility of the tabernacle
It signifies the Israelites’ dependence on Moses alone
questions.correctAnswer: It represents God’s continual guidance and presence during Israel’s wilderness journey
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:36-38 narrates the cloud by day and fire by night guiding Israel, showing God’s faithful presence that directs and accompanies His people throughout their pilgrimage, a key theme in redemptive history.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that rituals like anointing and setting up altars are mere superstition with no theological significance. What does Exodus 40:9-11 actually teach about these rituals?
options: They are divinely ordained acts that sanctify persons and objects for holy use
They are purely symbolic with no real effect
They are human inventions to control people
They are outdated practices irrelevant to worship
questions.correctAnswer: They are divinely ordained acts that sanctify persons and objects for holy use
questions.explanation: Verses 9-11 show God commanding Moses to anoint and sanctify the tabernacle and its vessels, teaching that these rituals are God-ordained means of consecration, not superstition, pointing to the holiness required in worship (cf. Hebrews 9:1-5).

questions.question: What attribute of God is emphasized by His glory filling the tabernacle and the cloud covering it, preventing Moses’ entry as stated in Exodus 40:34-35?
options: God’s transcendence and holiness
God’s mercy and forgiveness
God’s immanence and accessibility
God’s wrath and judgment
questions.correctAnswer: God’s transcendence and holiness
questions.explanation: The cloud and glory filling the tabernacle (Exodus 40:34-35) express God’s transcendence and holiness, emphasizing that He is wholly other and must be approached with reverence and awe (cf. Isaiah 6:1-5).

questions.question: How does Exodus 40:22-25 demonstrate the ordered nature of worship as instituted by God?
options: By prescribing specific placement and lighting of the table, bread, candlestick, and lamps
By allowing freeform worship without regulations
By emphasizing spontaneous prayer over ritual
By focusing solely on sacrifices without other elements
questions.correctAnswer: By prescribing specific placement and lighting of the table, bread, candlestick, and lamps
questions.explanation: Verses 22-25 detail the precise arrangement of the table with bread and the candlestick with lit lamps, demonstrating that God ordains an ordered and reverent form of worship involving both physical elements and symbolism.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight emerges from Exodus 40:6 and Exodus 40:29 regarding the altar of burnt offering?
options: The altar is the place of atonement and approach to God through sacrifice
The altar is only a decorative piece
The altar is a symbol of human effort for righteousness
The altar is unrelated to forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: The altar is the place of atonement and approach to God through sacrifice
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:6 commands setting the altar of burnt offering before the tabernacle, and 40:29 records offerings upon it, teaching that the altar is central for atonement and approach to God through sacrifice, pointing forward to Christ's ultimate sacrifice.

questions.question: According to Exodus 40:31-32, what theological principle is taught by Moses, Aaron, and his sons washing their hands and feet before entering the tent or approaching the altar?
options: The necessity of ritual cleansing to maintain holiness in approaching God
That physical cleanliness alone is sufficient for worship
That priests could enter the tent at any time without preparation
That washing symbolizes human merit before God
questions.correctAnswer: The necessity of ritual cleansing to maintain holiness in approaching God
questions.explanation: Verses 31-32 show the priests washing hands and feet before entering the tent or near the altar, teaching the principle that approaching a holy God requires ritual cleansing, symbolizing purity and separation from defilement.

questions.question: How does the erection of the court around the tabernacle (Exodus 40:8, 33) reflect God’s holiness and the need for separation?
options: It physically separates the holy space from the common, teaching separation from sin
It is purely for crowd control
It allows unrestricted access to the tabernacle
It symbolizes the unity of Israel without distinction
questions.correctAnswer: It physically separates the holy space from the common, teaching separation from sin
questions.explanation: The court set up around the tabernacle with hangings at the gate (Exodus 40:8,33) marks the boundary between holy and common, teaching that God's holiness requires separation from sin and the profane.

questions.question: What narrative arc is completed by Moses following all the LORD’s commands exactly as described in Exodus 40:16?
options: The faithful obedience of the mediator in establishing God’s dwelling with His people
The failure of Israel to obey God’s laws
The rejection of the tabernacle as unnecessary
The independence of Moses from God’s guidance
questions.correctAnswer: The faithful obedience of the mediator in establishing God’s dwelling with His people
questions.explanation: Exodus 40:16 emphasizes Moses' exact obedience to God’s commands, portraying him as the faithful mediator who faithfully sets up the tabernacle, symbolizing God’s presence dwelling with His people and advancing the redemption story.
